extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians/authors preparing and submitting research papers to the Canadian Journal of Mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing, submitting, and publishing full-length research papers to the Canadian Journal of Mathematics, covering formatting, required front matter, submission procedure, peer review criteria, copyright/Open Access options, and post-acceptance production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum paper length
rubrics_metrics.description: A research paper submitted to the Canadian Mathematical Journal (Journal) should be at least 18 pages long.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers lesser than 18 pages should instead be submitted to the Canadian Mathematical Bulletin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be written in English or French.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript final form and conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: It is vital that authors take care to ensure that the manuscript is in final form and that the paper conforms to the following specifications:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should prepare the paper to meet the listed formatting and front-matter requirements before submission (see subsequent items: title/abstract/MSC, bibliography format, class file, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: First page: title, authors, abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The first page should contain a short descriptive title, the name(s) of the author(s) followed by an abstract, not exceeding 200 words, which can be read independently of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract must be self-contained and ≤200 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: This [first-page material] should be followed by the Mathematics Subject Classification Number for the primary and secondary subjects of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide MSC codes for primary and secondary subjects immediately after the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author affiliation and contact placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The institutional affiliation and complete address of each author (including e-mail) should appear at the bottom of the last page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full postal addresses and e-mail addresses for all authors on the last page of the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography order and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations should be given in an alphabetical bibliography at the end of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a single alphabetical reference list (not numbered by appearance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference abbreviations and DOI inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of references should use the standard abbreviations issued by Mathematical Reviews (MR) and should include the DOI whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MR standard journal abbreviations and include DOIs where available (CrossRef can be used to find DOIs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the journal class file
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a specific class file for Journal papers which is available here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to use the journal's provided LaTeX class file for submission/production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format and system
rubrics_metrics.description: When the manuscript is in its final form, it should be submitted online, in PDF form, by clicking the Submit your article link here or the button above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EditFlow service is used to manage communications between the editors and authors; submit a PDF of the final-form manuscript for initial submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission system account requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You will need an account for the submission system, which is separate to your Cambridge Core account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For login and submission support, consult the submission and support pages before attempting to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are reviewed for suitability, importance of findings, and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After initial screening for these criteria, papers are sent to academic referee(s) unknown to the author(s) and expert in the appropriate subject area. Referees verify the scientific findings and may improve the clarity of the research; editors make the final publication decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous expert refereeing
rubrics_metrics.description: After screening, papers are sent to academic referee(s), unknown to the author(s), expert in the appropriate subject area and carefully chosen by the Editorial Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees verify findings and may suggest clarity improvements; editorial board selects referees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright Assignment Form (CAF) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The author will be required to complete and sign the Copyright Assignment Form (CAF) as part of the submission process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completing the CAF assigns copyright to the Canadian Mathematical Society (CMS), enabling CMS to legally publish the paper online and in print (see Standard Terms and Conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional Gold Open Access and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: When completing the CAF, the authors are also given the option to designate the paper for full public access (not requiring a subscription) in exchange for a one-time paper processing fee ($2,060 USD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the author declines Gold Open Access, the paper will be published using the traditional publishing model (available only to subscribers for the first five years). See Standard Terms and Conditions for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide source files after acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Cambridge University Press (the Publisher on behalf of the CMS) with a complete set of the most recent LaTeX source files (and any supplementary files required, such as figures or macros) and a PDF version of the resulting manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplying complete and up-to-date source and supplementary files is required for production after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted Manuscript assignment and posting
rubrics_metrics.description: After Cambridge receives the source files and copyright assignment, the submitted manuscript will be assigned a permanent DOI (Digital Object Identifier) and temporary headers and footers will be added. This version of the paper will be posted to the Journal's website in the 'Accepted Manuscripts' (AM) section and also emailed to the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting the AM makes the research available quickly; authors may be encouraged to post AM copies elsewhere (see Green Open Access).

rubrics_metrics.name: Green Open Access encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: We encourage authors to post a copy of the Accepted Manuscript version of the paper in arXiv, on their own institutional repositories, on other non-commercial repositories, or on their personal web sites in place of any previous versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Standard Terms and Conditions for any requirements or restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyediting and potential content changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the Accepted Manuscript has been posted online, Cambridge will copyedit and typeset the paper to finalize it for official online and print publication and ensure that the paper conforms to the layout and style of the publication. In some cases, the process may change the content of the paper (for example, to re-word portions or to improve clarity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that copyediting can alter wording; authors must check proofs carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs: author corrections and final approval
rubrics_metrics.description: During the process, a 'Proof' copy is sent to the communicating author for comments and corrections. Once corrections have been processed, the paper is reviewed for final approval and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly and thoroughly to proofs; the communicating author is responsible for checking and returning corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: FirstView publication and official publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When the paper is in final typeset form, the paper will be made available on the Journal’s web site FirstView section. The AM version will be simultaneously removed. The paper will remain in the FirstView section until it has been included in a print issue of the Journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that a Journal research paper is considered officially published when it appears online in FirstView.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print issue metadata updates
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Journal paper is included in a print issue, the online version is updated slightly to include the volume and issue number and the page numbers are re-assigned relative to the volume/issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the Journal’s web site, the paper moves from the FirstView section into the area dedicated to the new issue.
